description:
Implement the symmetric cert handshake — runCertHandshake() in clients/typescript/src/cert-auth.ts (sibling to auth.ts which holds the PSK handshake).

Mirror auth/cert.go runHandshake with clientFirst=true (we are always the client on the TS side):

1. Generate 32-byte random nonce (myNonce) via crypto.getRandomValues.
2. Send CertHello { cert: localCert, nonce: myNonce } via protodelim frame.
3. Read peer CertHandshakeMessage; require .hello variant.
4. Verify peer cert via cert.ts (ship-3pp.3) → peerClaim.
5. Check peer nonce length == 32. Otherwise ErrUnauthorized.
6. Sign 'mosey-cert-v1' || peerHello.nonce with localPriv → mySig.
7. Send CertHandshakeMessage { proof: SignedNonce { signature: mySig } }.
8. Read peer CertHandshakeMessage; require .proof variant.
9. Verify Ed25519(peerClaim.peer_pubkey, 'mosey-cert-v1' || myNonce, peerProof.signature). Mismatch = ErrUnauthorized.
10. Wait for the post-handshake ackOK byte (0x01), same as PSK — auth/wrap.go writes it for both backends.
11. Return Identity { label: peerClaim.label, caps: { owner, write: write||owner, resize: resize||owner } }.

Failure mode: any verification failure throws an error with the 'mosey/auth(cert):' prefix matching the Go side's errPrefixCert convention.

Depends on ship-3pp.2 (wire format) and ship-3pp.3 (verification).
title: TS client: cert handshake
